To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the local structure of the Al/Y/SiC/N nanopowder is described by XAS at A1 K-edge using fluorescence detection, which is a new technique in the field of Si3N4 based ceramics.

the local structure of the Al atoms in the pre-alloyed powders is similar to that of amorphous Si3N4, and that the annealed powders contain crystalline AIN and other disordered sites like AlO4 and AlN30.
the local structure of the A1 in the pre-alloyed A1/Y/SiCN powders evolves during annealing under N 2 towards that of AIN.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the local structure of new pre-alloyed phases of A1/Si/C/N system, in which A1 is substituted by the Y203 additive, by using XAS at the A1-K edge in the fluorescence yield detection mode.
a study of local structures of pre-alloying of SiCN nanopowders by XAS at A1-K edge.
the development of a new class of materials, namely SiCN ceramics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the local structure around A1 is not fully crystallized in the pre-alloyed powders and that a progressive evolution towards the crystalline structure is observed during annealing.
the A1 Kedge EXAFS spectra of the as-prepared and annealed pre-alloyed powders can be fitted by a model containing two shells, one at a distance of 1.91 A and the other at 2.78 A.
the A1 Kedge XANES and XES spectra are consistent with the presence of A1 in the form of AIN, A1N30 and A104, with a relative proportion that is not constant and evolves with temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the local structure around A1 in the pre-alloyed SiCN powders is similar to that of crystalline a-AlN and that the local environment of A1 in the as-prepared powders is more similar to a-AlN than a-SiAlON.

we have been able to show that the A1 local environment in the as-prepared powders can be described by a mixture of A1N and A1O2 sites, and that the A1 environment evolves during annealing towards A1N sites.
the local structure around A1 is strongly influenced by the local environment of Y and N atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the A1 local structure can be modified by using a pre-alloyed nanopowder.
the A1 Kedge fluorescence yield spectra of the amorphous phases can be described by a linear combination of the A1 K edge EXAFS spectra of the crystalline phases.
the local structure of the pre-alloyed powders is different from that of the corresponding crystalline phases.
